# Sirach Chapter 47 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 47 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**47:1** After him, Nathan rose up to prophesy in the days of David.

**47:2** As the fat is separated from the peace offering, so David was set apart from the children of Israel.

**47:3** He played with lions as with young goats, and with bears as with lambs of the flock.

**47:4** In his youth, did he not slay a giant and remove reproach from the people, when he swung his hand with a smooth stone and brought down the boastfulness of Goliath?

**47:5** For he called upon the Most High Lord, who gave strength to his right arm to strike down a mighty warrior and to raise high the horn of his people.

**47:6** So the women of Israel acclaimed him for his ten thousands and praised him to the skies.

**47:7** When he took up his armor and engaged in warfare, he drew the sword against the Philistines, and his hand made short work of many.

**47:8** Before engaging in any undertaking, he would set his hands aright and give thanks to the Holy One, the Most High, with words of glory.

**47:9** With his whole heart he sang praises and loved his Maker. He placed singers before the altar, and with their voices made sweet melody.

**47:10** He gave splendor to the festivals and arranged the sacred seasons in perfect order throughout the year, while they praised his holy name, and the sanctuary resounded from morning.

**47:11** The Lord forgave his sins and exalted his horn forever; he gave him a royal covenant and a throne of glory in Israel.

**47:12** After him rose a wise son who lived in security because of him.

**47:13** Solomon reigned in days of peace, for God gave him rest on every side, so that he might build a house for his name and prepare a sanctuary that would endure.

**47:14** How wise you were in your youth! You were filled with understanding like a river!

**47:15** Your soul covered the earth, and you filled it with riddling parables.

**47:16** Your name spread to far-off islands, and you were loved for the peace you brought.

**47:17** For your songs and proverbs and parables and explanations the peoples marveled at you.

**47:18** In the name of the Lord God, who is called the God of Israel, you gathered gold like tin and amassed silver like lead.

**47:19** But you laid yourself open to women, and by your body you were brought into subjection.

**47:20** You put a stain upon your honor and profaned your lineage, bringing wrath upon your children — and they were grieved because of your folly,

**47:21** so that the kingdom was divided and from Ephraim a rebel kingdom arose.

**47:22** But the Lord will not abandon his mercy, nor let any of his words fail; he will not blot out the posterity of his chosen one, nor destroy the line of him who loved him; so he gave a remnant to Jacob and a root to David out of his own stock.

**47:23** Solomon rested with his ancestors, and left behind one of his seed — Rehoboam, foolish in counsel and lacking in sense — who made the people turn away by his policy. Then Jeroboam son of Nebat led Israel into sin and put Ephraim on the path of transgression.

**47:24** Their sins became so great that they were driven from their land.

**47:25** For they pursued every kind of evil until vengeance caught up with them.
